title.narrative: Strengthening media to respond to environmental emergencies in Mexico

description.narrative:
In Mexico, in the last 20 years alone, the number of weather-related extreme events increased from 3.5 to 5.8 events per year, on average, affecting more than 557,000 people in the country, with storms and floods being the most prevalent. In a context where information is essential for emergency prevention and preparedness, as well as for disaster risk reduction, the national media ecosystem has a key role to play.
This initiative aims to structure a national program, through a pilot with selected media outlets, to strengthen the capacity of the media ecosystem to establish policies and practices on content and editorial standards during emergencies; design standard operating procedures, contingency plans and escalation systems for physical security in emergencies; and provide disaster preparedness training for media personnel, including indigenous and community media.
